conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Morning light seeps through the gaps in the curtains, casting a faint golden line on the carpet.

conversation.text: .st show Library

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player5>'s currently registered personal information is as follows:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The aroma of freshly baked croissants snakes its way from the corridor through the door crack.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Sniff

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Maintain the most standard routine. Wake up before 8, change clothes simply, then wait for companions in the lobby downstairs.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Good morning, Professor Bailan"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "If there's anything the French can be proud of"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Good morning, everyone. Today, let's first go to the library to look up information about that Count."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "It's their cooking"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Naturally, it's their culinary culture."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Pierre appears silently by the pillar, holding a silver tray with white gloves. "Guests, the head chef has specially prepared white truffle scrambled eggs for the distinguished guests of the Orient Express, using butter freshly delivered from Provence last night."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Thank you very much, then we won't stand on ceremony."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Regardless of the two impatient teammates, Mr. Gungnir thinks since he paid, he should eat.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go, get something to eat first."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Shows an expression of never having seen the world before.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Lazily ties the bow tie, takes out the napkin from the chest and prepares for the meal.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The glass windows filter the morning light into a champagne color, projecting onto the tablecloths; the roses at the center of each table bear morning dew. The light sound of silver knives on porcelain plates, the fine flow from coffee pot spouts, and a string trio echoing in the corner reach your ears.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Coffee, bread, scrambled eggs, salad—I am the person with the healthiest diet in the world, if I hadn't stuffed 4 breads and 3 servings of scrambled eggs.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Intends to find a glass of juice to drink.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Professor Bailan: Blood orange juice + a drop of absinthe. player4: Ginger honey sparkling water (for motion sickness prevention). player2: Chilled Muscat grape juice.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #A cup of black coffee without anything added is enough to sweep away the morning fatigue, restoring a full-blooded state. Professor Bailan savors the lava cake in front of him.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Pack a breakfast for the coachman.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Wipe the corner of the mouth.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: (gogogo)

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go, maybe the coachman is already waiting for us at the door."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I'm ready, let's go."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Lightning's mane gleamed in the morning light, clearly having been meticulously brushed. The coachman leaned against the carriage shaft, toying with a coin in his hand—exactly the tip player2 gave last night.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #awkwardly rubs nose

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Don't say that, my friend, have you had breakfast?" #waves the bread in hand

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The coachman's stomach let out a loud rumble at the perfect moment, and he embarrassedly rubbed his nose.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But things made by family are always better than others', aren't they?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There's an atmosphere called the feeling of home."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The coachman suddenly stopped adjusting the reins, his gaze softening. "What you said... is like my old buddy here—no fancy new saddle fits him as well as the pad made from my old coat." Then he suddenly laughed, pulling out a handkerchief embroidered with crooked letters from his pocket. "Look, my daughter stitched this... the needlework is messier than a spider's web, but if I ever forget to bring it—" He made a comical chest-leaking motion, but carefully folded the handkerchief and tucked it back inside his coat. "Even the north wind from Paris would dare bully me!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #tries to move past the topic after the coachman finishes breakfast "Then we should get going, right?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The carriage briskly turned the last corner, wheels rolling over newly laid pavement. "We're here!" He jumped down, boots crunching a patch of morning frost. "Going through the main gate would mean queuing until noon, but we—" He winked, pulling a brass key from his pocket and spinning it on his finger. "have a 'special passage.'"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #doesn't understand the language, but seems to grasp what's about to happen

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Ha, it seems I didn't misjudge you, Louis, you're truly a local expert."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Hey, this is my turf!" He proudly patted his chest.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #looks at player2 communicating fluently with the locals in French, feeling very impressed

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #follows Old Henry to quickly scram

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "What did he say?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Jean-Louis expertly led the three through a hidden side corridor, the air filled with the scent of parchment and oak bookshelves. Occasionally, librarians pushing carts laden with ancient books passed by; seeing him, they just nodded and smiled, clearly long accustomed to it.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #silently nods, indeed a correct decision.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "He said to let us leave quickly."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #follows closely behind

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Sunlight filtered through the glass, casting halos on the oak floor. Towering bookshelves stood like a maze, the air floating with scents of paper, ink, and old leather. Ladders leaned against the shelves, librarians pushed carts with brass wheels piled with books awaiting reshelving. The coachman stood at the threshold of the side door, hat tilted, spinning that coin in his hand. "Alright, lords, 'Lightning' is urging me back." "Lightning" stamped its hooves impatiently outside. He backed away while walking out.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #captivated by the sight of the library

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "About what time should I come back to pick you up?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #looks at Professor Bailan for opinion

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So many books."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Around 7 tonight should be fine, I think." #first takes out two-thirds of the fare

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: As Jean-Louis took the coins, his fingers quickly brushed against his lapel—ensuring sweat wouldn't dampen the bills—then made the coin somersault between his knuckles like a magic trick. "Your prepaid sincerity rings louder than the bells of Notre Dame!" Before he finished, "Lightning" suddenly grabbed his collar from behind and pulled. The coachman laughed heartily as he was dragged back to the driver's seat. "Alright then! Seven sharp—I'll have this old fellow come fetch you under the stars!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #pays respects to this coachman

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then the carriage quickly sped off.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Our Lightning needs to eat, doesn't it?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Look for information about the Count and that fragment.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Read Professor Smith's notes again.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Look for information about the Count's past and the location of his old residence.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you wish for, it will surely be answered. <player5>'s Library prayer:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Search for information related to the Sedifical statue and where it was taken during the Napoleonic Wars.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The Count's Villa

conversation.text: .ra Library

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you wish for, it will surely be answered. <player4>'s Library prayer:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player4 repeatedly scribbles over the spelling of Sedifical on an index card, ultimately mistakenly queries the Sadducal statue and rummages through military archives in the religious history section, drawing suspicious glances from the librarian. When old Marcel proactively asks if he needs help, he insists, "I can do it myself." Three hours later, when Professor Bailan easily finds the entry, player4 is staring blankly at the door sign—he never figured out the French classification label system and spent the afternoon fruitlessly searching through piles of architectural drawings.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Watching player4 stare blankly at the labels, turn to old Marcel beside him.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: It shouldn't be... The notes were very detailed... Damn French, what kind of broken language is this?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Old sir, my friend is quite stubborn, you know, a kid who just got into a PhD program tends to have a bit of an inflated ego."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Old Marcel lifts his cloudy gray eyes from above his reading glasses, the wrinkles at the corners of his mouth slowly folding into a knowing smile. "These young PhDs..." he mutters deliberately loud enough for player4 to hear, but his gnarled fingers have already deftly pulled out a leather-bound register.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you wish for, it will surely be answered. <player3>'s Library Use 80 prayer:

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Old Marcel, hunched over, drags out a package wrapped in mold-spotted parchment from the depths of the ancient book cabinet. As he unties the faded silk ribbon, dust dances in the beam of light.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Thank you." #Browse these books and then translate the contents for my two teammates who can understand what the books are saying.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Just now I noticed that lady was looking for this Count, so I took the liberty of investigating a bit."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Wow, you are truly an extremely competent librarian."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "As for the statue's whereabouts during the Napoleonic era, no relevant records were found. It was just personal luggage; such things wouldn't be mentioned in the library."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Prayer received! Continuing to record the horror of the Orient Express for you. Currently recorded texts: 1363, time elapsed: 7 hours, 5 minutes, 36 seconds.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: As the story last told,

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Shake Bailan and player4. "Friends, time to make a move."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Jean-Louis leans against the carriage shaft, an unlit cigarette dangling from his mouth. Seeing the three stumble over, he grins.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "They," #patting the two companions, "are indeed such people."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Lightning, let's go!" The whip cracks crisply in the air. "We'll take a shortcut—"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Dazed and confused.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "As a friend of mine once said, there are two kinds of people in the world: those who die from exhaustion and those who die from boredom. I think these two definitely aren't the second kind."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ah, it's not that serious. They probably won't work themselves to death. One must devote limited time to infinite work."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The carriage rolls over damp cobblestones, its wheels reflecting shimmering light under the gas street lamps. Lightning's horseshoe splashes water from a puddle, startling a stray cat at the alley entrance. When player4 wakes up groggily, he sees Jean-Louis driving with one hand, accepting a stolen butter roll from a bakery boy with the other. "Passing by the bakery's back alley, you can still snag a piece of freshly baked sourdough!" He winks.
